name: ISO/IEC 27017:2015
description: Code of practice for information security controls based on ISO/IEC 27002 for cloud services. Provides guidelines for both cloud service providers and cloud service customers.

controls.title: Shared roles and responsibilities within a cloud computing environment
controls.description: The roles and responsibilities of the cloud service provider and the cloud service customer shall be defined, documented, and communicated in the service agreement.

controls.title: Removal of cloud service customer assets
controls.description: The cloud service provider shall provide cloud service customers with the ability to extract all their data and ensure the data is deleted after withdrawal.

controls.title: Segregation in virtual computing environments
controls.description: The cloud service provider shall ensure that virtual computing environments are isolated from other virtual computing environments and from the management plane.

controls.title: Virtual machine hardening
controls.description: Virtual machines shall be hardened, in accordance with business needs, in a way that is consistent with procedures for physical end points.

controls.title: Administrator's operational security
controls.description: Cloud service providers shall ensure that all administrative operations are logged and reviewed on a regular basis.

controls.title: Monitoring of cloud services
controls.description: The cloud service provider shall make monitoring information available to cloud service customers relevant to their cloud computing environment.

controls.title: Alignment of security management for virtual and physical networks
controls.description: The cloud service provider shall implement controls to ensure that virtual networks are managed in a consistent manner with physical network controls.

controls.title: Business continuity for cloud service customers
controls.description: The cloud service provider shall provide cloud service customers with the information required for the customers to implement adequate business continuity management.
